excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content:
<@429719902363058177> from the conversation with 8298, I'm going to assume that the rationale for DFIing this is the same.

<@628018527470616606> / <@316280621783580673> you marked this as B, but 8298 as A. Do you have more details as to why?

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content: I guess one big downside of this is that ecrecover becomes stateful

excerpts.author: ben_a_adams
excerpts.content: As in we want it; but it could maybe wait a fork

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content: Do you think there is an issue with ecrecover being stateful?

excerpts.author: ben_a_adams
excerpts.content: Is only way to disable it (something valid needs to be flagged as invalid); which I assume is desired. Is just an account lookup and  a check of its code hash

excerpts.author: ben_a_adams
excerpts.content: So works with VOPS etc also

excerpts.author: ben_a_adams
excerpts.content: Also is just extending the already consensus tx rule that accounts with code cannot initiate txs to also be rule for ecrecover

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content: yeah I don't see any other way to do this tbh

excerpts.author: ben_a_adams
excerpts.content:
Team position

> Closes a real hole: an old key still approving transfers through a contract that can never be upgraded. We support the goal. The compatibility surface is the question, and it needs a scan of deployed bytecode before we would put it higher.
